findings.claim: Google token refresh persists the whole safeParse wrapper {success,data} as credential.key (default mode, sync off); next constructor googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at :75 throws, breaking Google Calendar after first refresh.
findings.evidence: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns safeParse result (_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29); base used .parse() which returned data. Zod repro (MP zt/check.js on zod 3.25.76; SP repro.cjs on zod 4.6.7) prints stored key {"success":true,"data":{...}} and next parse throws ZodError.
findings.reason: Executed repro by two seats; regression in default mode.

findings.claim: prisma used without import; resolves only via globalThis.prisma, which packages/prisma/index.ts:58-60 assigns only when NODE_ENV !== 'production', so getClient throws ReferenceError in production and every Salesforce operation fails.
findings.evidence: No prisma import in file (grep -c 'import prisma' = 0); type-checks via global declare in packages/prisma/index.ts:6-9. Reasoned, not executed.
findings.reason: Source citation from all four seats; production-only crash.

findings.claim: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but Google (res?.data), HubSpot (used as HubspotToken, Response persisted as key at :198), Zoho CRM (:217) and Zoho Bigin (:96) (tokenInfo.data.error) expect axios/gaxios/SDK shapes; sync refresh crashes or destroys the credential for these four integrations. response.ok is also never checked.
findings.evidence: fetch Response has no .data; refreshFunction typed () => any hides the mismatch. Reasoned from source.
findings.reason: Four seats agree; core purpose of the feature broken for 4 integrations and HubSpot credential overwritten.

findings.claim: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to '[object Object]' and collide; z.object strips unknown keys, so sync mode keeps only access_token and drops all expiry fields (Zoom expiry_date becomes NaN -> next zoomTokenSchema.parse fails permanently; Office365 refreshes on every call; Salesforce loses instance_url).
findings.evidence: node -e repro of key collapse; MP zod check prints {"success":true,"data":{"access_token":"a"}} for input with expiry_date/refresh_token; SP repro prints computed keys "[object Object]" "[object Object]".
findings.reason: Executed repro; sync-mode credential destruction for Zoom. Severities ranged Important-Critical; normalised to Critical for credential loss.

findings.claim: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token'; Office365 calendar (:264, schema marks refresh_token optional) and Zoom (:117-121, sync mode) persist it over the real refresh token, causing permanent invalid_grant.
findings.evidence: Before patch the key was absent and the stored token survived the spread. Reasoned plus zod repro output.
findings.reason: Three correctness/spec seats agree; credential loss in default mode for Office365 when Microsoft omits refresh_token.

findings.claim: Webhook looks up appStoreMetadata[app.slug], but appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name, not slug; google-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, zoom, lark-calendar return 404 'App not found'.
findings.evidence: packages/app-store/apps.metadata.generated.ts:98,109,110,146 keys googlecalendar/office365calendar/office365video/zoomvideo vs slugs in each _metadata.ts (e.g. googlecalendar/_metadata.ts:17 slug 'google-calendar'). getAppFromSlug (packages/app-store/utils.ts:123) does the correct lookup. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Source citation; webhook unusable for most integrations the patch wires up.

findings.claim: credentialId passed as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens(fn, appSlug, userId); sync endpoint receives calcomUserId=<credential id> and may return another user's tokens; userId guard bypassed for team credentials.
findings.evidence: Signature at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3; every other caller passes credential.userId. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Cross-user token confusion in sync mode.

findings.claim: getClient performs an unconditional token refresh on every construction (every booking), persists the new token but builds jsforce.Connection with the stale credentialKey.access_token (:104), bypasses refreshOAuthTokens so sync mode never applies, uses fragile response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok, hard-codes login.salesforce.com (sandbox orgs fail), and has a dead !success branch.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from source; jsforce Connection already receives clientId/clientSecret/refreshToken (auto-refresh not confirmed, node_modules absent).
findings.reason: Four seats agree; extra network call per booking and contradicts sync intent.

findings.claim: Slug sent to sync endpoint is 'zoomvideo' but the app slug is 'zoom' (zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16); the webhook resolves apps by prisma.app.slug, so outbound and inbound halves of the protocol name Zoom differently.
findings.evidence: grep slug zoomvideo/_metadata.ts -> 'zoom'; other hard-coded slugs match their config. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Source citation; SP rated Minor, OCR/MP Important; normalised to Important.

findings.claim: Outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no secret/signature, only calcomUserId and appSlug; the parent app cannot authenticate Cal.com before returning live access tokens.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from source; CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET exists but is not sent.
findings.reason: Unverified: protocol decision with the external endpoint owner; settle by agreeing an auth header contract and asserting it in an integration test against a stub endpoint.

findings.claim: No tests for the new credential-writing webhook or for the shared refresh/parse helpers; an integration test would have caught the Google key-shape, sync shape mismatch, minimum-schema and slug-lookup bugs.
findings.evidence: No test files in the patch (git diff --stat). Reasoned.
findings.reason: Red tests written in the fix step for each accepted finding close this gap.

findings.claim: schema.parse(req.body), JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) are unguarded: malformed body, bad ciphertext or wrong key yields 500 instead of 400; decrypted keys are not shape-validated before being written to credential.key.
findings.evidence: Lines 31, 57-59. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Cheap input-validation fix at a trust boundary.

findings.claim: Webhook secret compared with !== (not constant-time) and no req.method restriction on a credential-write endpoint.
findings.evidence: Reasoned; crypto.timingSafeEqual is the standard fix.
findings.reason: Hardening at trust boundary; small change.

findings.claim: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure yet returns a safeParse wrapper, so .success checks are dead (office365 :264, zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:104-106, salesforce :91-94); office365's console.error of the failing MS response was removed and the thrown error has no zod detail.
findings.evidence: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-29. Reasoned.

findings.reason: ponytail: no behavioural impact; tidy when the helpers are next touched.
